properties.name: The five holes are one hole: six of eleven constructors cannot write ANY prose about the thing they create, because the class was fixed one report at a time and never swept
properties.statement:
RUN AS THE SKILL ON REQUEST, 2026-09-07. Anthony asked, on being shown five newly visible unreachable properties: "should we run /root-cause on these 5 holes to see if it is something deeper?" It is.

STEP 1 - THE OBSERVATION. Five properties the reachability gate reported as newly visible once its cross-type leak was closed: Actor.description, Interface.description, Release.description, Resource.description, DesignEpoch.checksum. Four of the five are the SAME FIELD NAME on four different types, which is a pattern rather than four coincidences.

STEP 3 - CANDIDATES, generated from the surface and the schema rather than from memory:
(a) Coincidence; four independent omissions.
(b) The property was declared on those types AFTER their constructors were written, and nothing checks.
(c) Those types keep their prose in a DIFFERENT field, which their constructors do take, so description is genuinely redundant on them - the shape of chg:accept-0500fc47eb120e13, where a Component stores prose as `purpose` and add_component's resolver wrongly asked for `description`.
(d) The class was fixed one report at a time, wherever somebody hit it, and never swept.

STEP 4 AND 5 - THE MEASUREMENTS.
(c) IS REFUTED, and this is the finding that matters. Of the eleven types declaring `description`, six have a constructor that does not take it - Artifact, Environment, Interface, Project, Release, Resource - and for every one of those six, `description` IS THE ONLY PROSE FIELD THE TYPE DECLARES. None of the six takes statement, purpose, summary or any other prose parameter either. So on six of eleven types the surface lets a user NAME a thing and never SAY WHAT IT IS, except through the generic escape hatch. That is a bigger and simpler statement than five scattered holes.

(d) IS SUPPORTED BY THE HISTORY. Walking every commit that touched service.rs: CapabilityReq carried `description` from 2026-07-18, at its introduction; ContributorReq from 2026-07-22, likewise. VerificationReq DID NOT - it gained one on 2026-08-17, in a commit named "A check records what it FOUND separately from what it IS". That is precisely the founding case this project's own reachability instrument records in its docstring: Verification.description declared, fulltext, the type's embedding field, used ONCE in 164 nodes because add_verification had no parameter for it. So the hole was found, reported, and fixed ON THAT ONE TYPE. Nobody asked which other types had it, and nothing could answer if they had - the instrument that would have said so was itself hiding these six behind the fused filter fixed earlier today.

STEP 6 - THE CLASS, and it is the skill's own test: would the fix have stopped the earlier occurrences? Adding a parameter to add_interface stops today's. The CAUSE is that a vocabulary hole is fixed where it is reported and the same question is never asked of the sibling types, so the class survives every instance fix. That is the same shape as the sequence-hint defect recurring on plan_epoch after being fixed in add_epoch, and the same shape as the leak in the reachability map fixed hours ago, where only the tools named add_* were mapped and every setter leaked. Three instances of one habit in one day.

A SECOND STRUCTURAL FINDING, from the same sweep and not asked for: NINE OF 29 NODE TYPES HAVE NO TYPED WRITE TOOL AT ALL - Actor, Anchor, DimensionAssessment, DimensionObservation, DriftEvent, EnvironmentRule, Fragment, QualityGate, Snapshot. Several are correctly machine-written (Fragment, Snapshot, DriftEvent and the two Dimension types are produced by other operations), but Actor, EnvironmentRule and QualityGate are vocabulary a user would reasonably want to write, and Actor is why Actor.description cannot simply be given a parameter: there is no add_actor to give it to. This is the same class as fact:defect-designrule-has-no-constructor-reported-by-two-independent-projects, which two projects reported independently.

STEP 9 - WHAT IS NOT ESTABLISHED. Whether each of the six types SHOULD carry prose is a judgement, not a measurement; the reporter wanted it on two types and nobody has been asked about the rest. Whether the three user-facing types with no constructor should get one is a bigger question than this record settles. And the history walk read service.rs only, so a struct that moved to another file in the BL-181 split may have gained its parameter somewhere this measurement could not see - FlowReq and AddEpochReq both returned no date for that reason, and neither conclusion above rests on them.
